primaryText: If it rains tomorrow there will not be a terrific cloudburst. If there is a terrific cloudburst tomorrow it will not rain.
discourseSegments: If it rains tomorrow there will not be a terrific cloudburst.
If there is a terrific cloudburst tomorrow it will not rain.
comment: One might accept and affirm the first but not infer the second. Quoted in running text, here capitalized and punctuated as utterances.

primaryText: Either it will rain or it will snow in Berkeley next year. If it doesn't rain then it will snow in Berkeley next year.
discourseSegments: Either it will rain or it will snow in Berkeley next year.
If it doesn't rain then it will snow in Berkeley next year.
comment: Paradoxical to infer the second from the first. Quoted in running text, here capitalized and punctuated as utterances.

primaryText: If Smith dies before the election Jones will win. If Jones wins then Smith will retire. If Smith dies before the election he will retire.
discourseSegments: If Smith dies before the election Jones will win.
If Jones wins then Smith will retire.
If Smith dies before the election he will retire.
context: Smith and Jones are the only candidates for a public office of which Smith is the incumbent, and Smith has announced his intention of retiring to private life in the event of his defeat.
comment: Proper to affirm the first two, obviously irrational to infer the third. Quoted in running text, here capitalized and punctuated as utterances.

primaryText: If Jones wins the election then Smith will retire. If Smith dies before the election and Jones wins then Smith will retire.
discourseSegments: If Jones wins the election then Smith will retire.
If Smith dies before the election and Jones wins then Smith will retire.
context: Smith and Jones are the only candidates for a public office of which Smith is the incumbent, and Smith has announced his intention of retiring to private life in the event of his defeat.
comment: One might affirm the first, but it would be absurd to infer the second. Quoted in running text, here capitalized and punctuated as utterances.
